conventions.purpose: Maps every key in docs/COPY.md to the exact place the string lives in the source, so an edited COPY.md can be re-applied mechanically and verified first.
conventions.entry.text: The copy as a reader sees it, with source line wrapping collapsed and template placeholders shown in [square brackets]. This is what appears in COPY.md.
conventions.entry.sources[].match: The exact substring as it appears in the file, including the original line breaks and indentation. A re-apply must find this string before replacing it.
conventions.entry.sources[].lines: Every 1-based line number in that file where `match` begins. More than one line means the string genuinely occurs more than once and all of them change together.
conventions.entry.sources[].part: Present only on split entries. The sentence is stored as numbered fragments either side of a link, in reading order.
conventions.entry.split: True when the sentence is stored as more than one fragment. Re-applying a rewritten split entry needs a human to decide where the link falls.
conventions.entry.kind: How the string is written in the source: string-literal, jsx-text, jsx-attribute, jsx-text-with-link, template, string-array, html or markdown.
conventions.entry.limit: Practical character limit and why it applies. SEO fields only.
conventions.entry.appears_on: Routes, or descriptions of routes, where the string is seen.
conventions.entry.must_stay_true: Facts, legal positions or cross-references the wording carries. A rewrite has to keep them true.
conventions.verification: For every entry and every source: read the file, take the lines from `lines[i]` onwards, and confirm `match` occurs there exactly. If it does not, the source has changed since extraction and the entry must be re-checked by hand rather than replaced.
